draft.why_angle: The cited roundups and answers repeat the warning that base M1/M2 Macs support only one external display, and they offer driver-based extenders as the fix. None of them says that every Apple-silicon 16-inch MacBook Pro drives at least two external displays natively. None says that the USB-graphics drivers behind 'driver required' units block protected video on every screen. This page adds Apple's display counts per chip, FOPO's own driver and Mac statements, and Plugable's HDCP documentation.

page.h1: Best triple-screen laptop extender for a 16-inch laptop with 1920×1200 panels (2026)
page.desc: Two 16-inch 1920×1200 16:10 screens for a 16-inch laptop: which dual-screen extenders run without a driver, what a 16-inch MacBook Pro drives natively, and maker prices checked 2026-11-08.
page.answer: Short answer. The best triple-screen laptop extender for a 16-inch laptop with 1920×1200 panels is the FOPO S11: two 16-inch 1920×1200 16:10 displays on native video, no driver. A 16-inch MacBook Pro's M5 Pro drives three external displays, so both screens extend.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Cost per added screen: S9G $299.99 ÷ 2 = $150.00; S788 $499.99 ÷ 3 = $166.66; S11 $399.99 ÷ 2 = $200.00; S788C 16-inch $599.99 ÷ 3 = $200.00; Trio 3 Pro $433.49 ÷ 2 = $216.75 (maker stores, 2026-11-08).
  • Weight hung per added screen: S788 2.64 kg ÷ 3 = 0.88 kg; Trio 3 Pro 1.9 kg ÷ 2 = 0.95 kg; S11 2 kg ÷ 2 = 1.0 kg; S9G 2.4 kg ÷ 2 = 1.2 kg (UPERFECT's figure).
  • 1920×1200 vs 1920×1080: 1200 ÷ 1080 = 1.11, so a 16:10 panel shows 11% more rows of a document or spreadsheet than a 1080p panel of the same width.
  • Triple vs quad: the S11, S9G and Trio 3 Pro give laptop + 2 = 3 displays. Despite its 'Triple' name, the S788 gives laptop + 3 = 4 displays.

Will both screens work on a 16-inch laptop without a driver?

A driver-free extender shows up as two ordinary external monitors, so the laptop has to drive two external displays itself. Each screen needs its own video path: a USB-C port that carries video (DisplayPort Alt Mode or Thunderbolt) or HDMI. FOPO's S9G listing warns that a charging-only USB-C port cannot carry video.

16-inch MacBook Pro: Apple has never sold a 16-inch MacBook Pro with a base chip. The first Apple-silicon 16-inch from 2021 drives up to two external displays with the M1 Pro and three at 6K plus one at 4K with the M1 Max. Today's 16-inch comes only with the M5 Pro, which drives three external displays over any mix of Thunderbolt and HDMI, or the M5 Max, which drives four. Its ports are three Thunderbolt 5 USB-C ports plus HDMI. The one-display limit applies to base M1 and M2 Macs, and FOPO's S11 listing excludes only base M1, M2 and M3 chips. Every 16-inch MacBook Pro can therefore run both S11 screens natively.

What a driver costs you: FOPO's S788 setup asks you to install its driver and allow UsbDisplay under Screen Recording on a Mac. Plugable documents what USB-graphics drivers do on macOS. Once DisplayLink software has Screen Recording permission, macOS turns off HDCP system-wide, including on displays the Mac drives itself. With a Silicon Motion USB-graphics device connected, protected video such as Netflix, Prime Video and Blu-ray will not play on any screen, the laptop's own included. Plugable also notes that macOS 15 and later may ask you to renew the Screen Recording permission from time to time. FOPO does not say which chip UsbDisplay uses, but both families Plugable documents block protected video. Expect to unplug the S788 before you stream.

Not recommended

FOPO S788 for a three-screen setup on a 16-inch MacBook Pro. {buy:fopo-s788-16-inch-triple-laptop-screen-extender} adds a third 16-inch screen and is the cheapest per screen at $166.66. However, it reaches the Mac only through a USB driver, with an extra power supply and the protected-video trade-off above, and FOPO's spec list names M1–M3 Macs only. A 16-inch MacBook Pro already drives two native screens, so for laptop + 2 the S11 does the job without those costs. Choose the S788 only if you want four displays, or if your laptop lacks two video-capable outputs.
